_README: Price-per-unit for every vendor/unit a single Cutline job can consume.
TWO DIFFERENT FIELDS, AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS:
verifiedPriceUsd    - a real vendor rate card price that a human has checked.
null everywhere in this file. NOTHING here has been verified
against a vendor invoice or rate card.
codeAssumedPriceUsd - the number THIS REPO currently bills against, with the
file:line it lives at. This is what the product already
believes. It is NOT evidence of the real price.
Do not collapse these two fields. A codeAssumedPriceUsd that turns out to be wrong
is exactly how a margin model silently lies.
scripts/cost-model.ts reads verifiedPriceUsd by default and refuses to present a
total as complete while any of them is null. Pass --use-code-assumptions to get a
provisional figure from codeAssumedPriceUsd instead; it is labelled PROVISIONAL.

meta.repoRevision: working tree with uncommitted changes; see docs/cost-audit.md
meta.howToVerify: Open each vendor's pricing page or a recent invoice, fill verifiedPriceUsd, set pricesVerified true.

llm_per_1k_tokens.TODO: Get the per-1M input AND output price for anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5 from the OpenRouter model page, plus OpenRouter's routing fee. Split into two entries if input/output differ.
llm_per_1k_tokens.codeAssumptionSource: src/lib/cost/pricing.ts (SERVICE_COSTS.LLM_PER_1K_TOKENS: 0.00025). Since Anthropic became the primary provider this rate feeds only the pre-job admission estimate (estimateCostUsd x ESTIMATED_LLM_TOKENS 4800).
llm_per_1k_tokens.envOverride: none. COST_PER_1K_TOKENS was read only by CostTracker.recordLlmTokens, which is gone.
llm_per_1k_tokens.modelSource: src/lib/pipeline/modelFallback.ts (DEFAULT_MODEL); OpenRouter is now the fallback after Anthropic
llm_per_1k_tokens.notes: The job's cost tracker no longer uses a blended rate. Each LLM call is booked from the usage the provider returns (src/lib/llm/chat.ts -> CostTracker.recordLlmCall): an OpenRouter call at OpenRouter's own usage.cost, an Anthropic call at the per-model input/output rates in src/lib/cost/llmPricing.ts. OpenRouter's fee on buying credits (about 5.5% by card) is not included.

llm_output_per_1m_tokens.TODO: Same check as the input rate.
llm_output_per_1m_tokens.notes: Booked per call from the input_tokens and output_tokens Anthropic returns. Prompts over 100,000 tokens pay $0.50 / $2.50. A model missing from CLAUDE_RATES is booked at $10 / $50 per million tokens, never $0, and logged once.

tts_per_character.TODO: ElevenLabs bills per CHARACTER on a subscription character quota. Get the effective $/character for the plan in use (plan quota / plan price), for model eleven_multilingual_v2.
tts_per_character.codeAssumptionSource: NONE - the repo has no per-character rate anywhere.
tts_per_character.notes: THIS IS THE UNIT THE VENDOR ACTUALLY BILLS, and the repo does not model it at all. See tts_per_second below.

tts_per_second.TODO: Do not fill this in as if it were a vendor price - it is not a unit ElevenLabs sells. Either derive it (chars-per-second x $/char) or migrate the tracker to characters.
tts_per_second.notes: UNIT MISMATCH. The tracker records seconds of OUTPUT audio (recordTtsSeconds, src/lib/cost/costEstimator.ts:19, fed from r.durationMs/1000 at src/lib/pipeline/orchestrator.ts:885 and :1530). ElevenLabs charges for INPUT characters. These diverge with speaking rate, and the divergence is systematic rather than noise.

video_per_second.TODO: Confirm against the GCP billing console that calls bill under the Veo 3.1 Fast video + audio 720p SKU. Re-check whenever VEO_MODEL, resolution or generateAudio changes: each is a different SKU (the standard model is $0.40/s with audio).
video_per_second.codeAssumptionSource: src/lib/cost/pricing.ts:2 (VEO_PER_SECOND: 0.10). Google's list price for Veo 3.1 Fast, video + audio, 720p, at cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/pricing, read 2026-10-25.
video_per_second.modelSource: src/lib/veo/index.ts:11 (VEO_MODEL default; the VEO_MODEL env var overrides it)

requestShape.resolution: not sent, so Veo's default of 720p
requestShape.generateAudio: not sent; audio is on, since the clips speak their lines

billingGranularity.notes: Every Veo call buys a fixed 8 seconds. A 9-second requirement costs 16 seconds. The estimator models this via VEO_CHUNK_SECONDS = 8 (src/lib/cost/pricing.ts:29).

video_per_second.notes: By far the largest single line item. At the code-assumed rate, 8 seconds costs $0.80. Until 2026-10-25 the code booked $0.40/s, the standard model's video + audio price, so Veo costs recorded on earlier jobs are 4x too high.

avatar_video_generation.unit: UNKNOWN - the code does not reveal HeyGen's billing unit (per video? per second? per credit?)
avatar_video_generation.TODO: Check the HeyGen plan in use. Determine (a) the billing unit, (b) whether stored Photo Avatars cost anything at rest, (c) whether a failed or discarded generation is still billed.
avatar_video_generation.codeAssumptionSource: NONE. Superseded by avatar_video_per_second below, which is the unit the tracker now meters (CostTracker.recordHeygenSeconds).
avatar_video_generation.notes: CONSEQUENCE: every HeyGen avatar render books $0 against the margin ceiling. The only HeyGen limit the code knows about is a stored-avatar cap inferred from error code 401028 (the number 3 is NOT in the code; an earlier revision of this file asserted it) (src/lib/lipsync/heygen.ts:266).

avatar_video_per_second.TODO: THIS IS THE BLOCKING UNKNOWN for talking-character margin. HeyGen may not even sell per-second - check whether the plan bills per video, per credit, or per minute, and convert to $/second of output. Until this is a number, HeyGen renders are invisible to the gross-margin ceiling.
avatar_video_per_second.codeAssumptionSource: src/lib/cost/pricing.ts HEYGEN_PER_SECOND = null. DELIBERATELY null, not a guess.
avatar_video_per_second.notes: The metering unit the code now uses. heygenRatePerSecond() returns 0 and logs an error once per process while this is unknown, and CostTracker.recordHeygenSeconds books against it. Before this entry existed HeyGen output was fed through recordVideoSeconds and priced at Google Veo rate ($0.40/s) - a confident number for the wrong vendor. $0.00 with a loud log is the honest placeholder; do NOT fill this in with Veo rate.

stored_photo_avatar.unit: 1 stored Photo Avatar (account-wide, cap of 3 on lower tiers)
stored_photo_avatar.TODO: Confirm the stored-avatar cap and whether higher tiers raise it; the cap is inferred from an error code, not read from an API.
stored_photo_avatar.notes: Content-addressed SHA-256 cache avoids re-uploading identical images (src/lib/lipsync/heygenPhotoCache.ts:34), so this is one of the few genuinely cached vendor calls in the codebase.

image_search_request.notes: First link in the image fallback chain (src/lib/images/source.ts). Because only DALL-E calls reach recordImageCalls, a job served entirely from Unsplash books $0 of image cost - which is right if the tier is free and wrong if it is not.

image_search_request.notes: Second link in the fallback chain, tried after Unsplash fails.

storage_gb_month.TODO: Get Vercel Blob storage $/GB-month from the Vercel pricing page and the plan's included allowance.
storage_gb_month.codeAssumptionSource: NONE - storage is not modelled anywhere in the cost tracker.
storage_gb_month.notes: Residency is per plan, not a month: the hourly cleanup deletes blobs under videos/ once they pass their owner's window - 24h on Free, 90 days on paid (src/lib/plans.ts, applied in src/lib/storage/publish.ts cleanupExpiredBlobs). VIDEO_RETENTION_HOURS overrides both with one flat window. A GB-month rate overstates Free badly and now understates a paid library that is retained for three months.

bandwidth_gb.notes: UNKNOWN mean file size - see docs/cost-audit.md. MAX_VIDEO_OUTPUT_MB is unset by default (src/lib/config/limits.ts:13-19), so nothing in the repo bounds it.

cpu_second.TODO: Get the host's $/hour or $/GB-hour for the instance size actually running the worker, then divide to a per-second rate.
cpu_second.codeAssumptionSource: NONE - render compute is not modelled in the cost tracker at all.
cpu_second.notes: This is a real per-job cost that the margin ceiling completely ignores. The container is billed continuously whether or not it is rendering, so a per-second rate only makes sense divided across actual throughput. See docs/cost-audit.md Part 1 for the render-time UNKNOWN.

command.notes: Not per-job in any clean sense: status polling dominates command volume, and it scales with viewers x queue depth rather than with renders.

compute_hour.TODO: Get Neon's compute-hour and storage pricing for the branch in use.
compute_hour.notes: A handful of queries per job; expected to be a rounding error next to Veo, but unmodelled.

transaction.TODO: Get Dodo's percentage + fixed fee per transaction. This reduces NET revenue per seat and therefore the true margin, which the ceiling in src/lib/cost/budget.ts does not account for.
transaction.notes: Not a per-job cost, but it belongs in a margin model: the budget ceiling is derived from LIST price (src/lib/cost/budget.ts PLAN_PRICE_USD), not from what actually lands in the bank.
